about: The threads of the Atlas timeline: named storylines that run across the ages. An annals event names the threads it belongs to in "threads": [id, ...]. Writers add threads through the lead; a new thread needs an id (lower-case words joined by hyphens), its Dia-thìris name (dt, which passes rodais_engine.normalize() and check_agreement(), and agrees with eras/NAMES.json), an English gloss, a colour and one sentence of description. status: canon (the name is attested in the master record) or proposed (the name awaits the lead's confirmation against NAMES.json).

threads.description: Neachdan the mason and his descendants, from the first fire to the end of the line.

threads.gloss: the mason's fire, the first fire
threads.description: The fire Neachdan carried home from the lightning-struck vein, and every hearth lit from it, kept or covered, from the first night to the grove.
Aisling and her line, as the copyists kept it.
The seven coals of the vein: their finding, their lighting, their rule and their failing.
The Stone Kings of the Age of Ailean and what was remembered of them.
The Roinn: the sharing of the land among the heirs and the shares' long history.
The promise of Coimhdeach na Fine, the Keeper of the Kin, and how it was kept or broken.
The coal-blooded: who carried the coal in their blood, and what became of them.
The humans' faith on the island, from the first chapel to the Church of the present day.
An Cogadh Fada, the Long War of the Age of Dubhan: its causes, campaigns and peace.
The Library at Muileann chaol and the record it keeps.
The humans' Company: its charter, camps, quays and coal ships.
Manannan's mist, which hid the island from the ships beyond it, and its thinning.
The Tuathaich: their homeland, their shires and their part in the Kingdom.

threads.gloss: the orders of the Old Faith
threads.description: The orders of An Creideamh Sean, the Old Faith: their founding, rules and quarrels.
Dubhan's fuel: its first making, its taking-up by the kingdom, its guild, its tithe and its export.

The fleet that sailed into the mist and never came back, the island left alone in the world, and the long learning to live cut off: the numbering of the ships, the empty places laid, the watch on the headlands and its lapsing.

The custodian houses of the vein, their rolls and their lots, from the first houses made after the Sundering through the crown joined to the vein, to the council of the seven heads that sat in the empty chair's stead.

threads.gloss: the Law of the Small Burning
threads.description: The rule that the vein-coal be burned only in small measure and only by the custodians, first written in the custody-book at the vein-house and kept, argued and bent through the whole Age of Sundering.
The thinning of the vein, from the first quiet note of the survey to the one sheet and the flooded galleries of the Age of the Kingdom.
The fading of the long lives of Ailean Mòr's blood, from heirs who counted their years in thousands to rulers who died at the ordinary span of every other household.
The roll of the Keepers of the bound flame at Dùn ìseal, from Beathag Bhàn to Catrìona nic Mhuirich, and the house that came to hold the watching of it.
The roads, waypoint houses, bridges and road-guards of the Holy Age, and the peace that the hearth-sign kept along them.
The people before the Dia-thìrich, their middens, towers, tally-stones and graves, and how the godkin's households met, traded with and outlasted them.
The yearly meeting of salt and wool at the ford below the Red Hill, from Raghnall Ceannfhionn's wading to the great gathering of the three thousandth year.
